problem: Find the surface area of the part of the surface $z=9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ that is subject to the constraint ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9.$
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/d2774aa4a85d25c4e35f3eb327adc82f9ef02eceb2be31ddf730493797e4cac2.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(-2x)^{2}+(-2y)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+4{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+4({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region $D$ can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula for polar coordinates, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+4({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\sqrt{1+4{r}^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}r\sqrt{1+4{r}^{2}}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta {\int }_{0}^{3}r\sqrt{1+4{r}^{2}}\,\text{d}r \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}r\sqrt{1+4{r}^{2}}\,\text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=1+4{r}^{2},$ we get $\text{d}u=8r\,\text{d}r.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & 0 & 3 \\ u & 1 & 37\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}r\sqrt{1+4{r}^{2}}\,\text{d}r & =2\pi \cdot \frac{1}{8}{\int }_{1}^{37}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}{\int }_{1}^{37}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{[{u}^{3/2}]}_{1}^{37} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}{[{u}^{3/2}]}_{1}^{37} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}[(37)^{3/2}-1] \\  & =\frac{\pi (37\sqrt{37}-1)}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
